records.record: Draft US-VOTE [1] failed with nine votes for, three against, and three abstentions [2] because China and Russia opposed it [3], while Draft RU-VOTE [4] failed with four votes for, seven against, and four abstentions [5] due to insufficient support [6]. The US approach favored international-observed elections and unhindered aid [7], whereas the Russian draft promoted the Montevideo Mechanism dialogue and government-led assistance [8]. Neither draft conferred authority. Analytical Suggestion: Reconcile electoral legitimacy with inclusive dialogue mechanisms.

evidence.US-VOTE: On 28 February 2019 the United States submitted S/2019/186. It received nine votes in favour, three against and three abstentions. China and the Russian Federation voted against it as permanent members, and the draft was not adopted.
evidence.RU-VOTE: S/2019/190 was a separate Russian draft. It received four votes in favour, seven against and four abstentions and failed to reach the required number of affirmative votes.
evidence.US-TEXT: The U.S. draft called for a peaceful process toward credible presidential elections under international observation. It proposed unhindered humanitarian access and assistance across Venezuela consistent with humanitarian principles.
evidence.RU-TEXT: The Russian draft supported inclusive national dialogue, including the Montevideo Mechanism. It placed Venezuela’s Government in the lead on humanitarian assistance and called for its consent and appeal.
